design:
D1. Navigation owns selection and starting. Conversation switching, new conversation and agent settings live in navigation (row menus, URL-backed destinations); the conversation header keeps only turn-level controls. There is no overflow menu.

D2. Destinations are named by AgentWeave ids (project id, conversation id), never by a provider session id, so a reload or back/forward restores the same place whatever the provider does.

D3. Rail chrome stays in hub-workspace-shell; this capability owns what the navigation lists and how a conversation is reached from it.
lifecycle: Split out of agent-conversation-workspace in the 2026-10-08 spec overhaul.
problem: An operator running several agents across several projects needs to see at a glance which conversation is working or waiting on them, and reach it in one action, without one project's conversations or drafts leaking into another's view.

requirements.rationale: Reading the conversation is the reason for selecting the agent; any intermediate step is a click that carries no information.
requirements.statement: Selecting an agent from navigation or from the project overview's agent roster SHALL open that agent's conversation directly, with no intermediate agent list, filter tab bar or selection placeholder.

requirements.rationale: Expanding to look and opening to go are different intents, and one control cannot express both.
requirements.statement: Navigation SHALL list every registered project as a named entry whose children are its agents, and each agent as an entry whose children are its conversations; a project's or agent's name and its expander SHALL be separately activatable, the name navigating and the expander toggling without navigating.

requirements.rationale: The conversation header carries a back-to-project control so the operator never has to find the project in navigation to leave a conversation.
requirements.statement: From an open agent conversation, the containing project's overview SHALL be reachable in a single action.

requirements.rationale: Agents are listed in the tree and peer traffic is merged into each conversation's timeline, so separate destinations would only duplicate them.
requirements.statement: Navigation MUST NOT offer an *Agents* destination or a *Messages* destination; the agent and message records and their APIs remain unchanged.

requirements.rationale: One local Hub owns many projects; every piece of client state is keyed by project id.
requirements.statement: Navigation SHALL read its project and agent tree from the collection of every registered project, SHALL let the operator open an existing directory, create a new project and switch projects without changing credentials, and MUST NOT leak conversations, drafts, cached server state or in-flight results across projects.

requirements.rationale: A destination the operator cannot reload or link to is not a place they can return to.
requirements.statement: Project, agent, conversation and settings navigation SHALL be represented in the browser URL using project id and AgentWeave conversation id, and reload and back/forward SHALL restore the represented destination; provider session identifiers MUST NOT be used as URL identity.

requirements.rationale: A silent cut-off reads as data loss; an unbounded list buries the agent rows below it.
requirements.statement: Navigation SHALL list an agent's open conversations beneath it, most recent activity first, each labelled by its title and marked when a peer started it; activating the agent's name SHALL open its most recent conversation, and beyond 7 conversations the rest SHALL sit behind an expander that states how many are hidden.

requirements.rationale: The tree costs a level of hierarchy; the recency view recovers the flat scan without losing which agent owns each thread.
requirements.statement: Navigation SHALL offer a recency view listing the project's open conversations across all agents, most recent first, each with its agent's identity colour as a leading edge; the agent tree SHALL be the default, the chosen view SHALL persist across reloads, archived conversations SHALL be reachable through a control stating their count, and beyond 15 conversations the rest SHALL sit behind an expander stating how many are hidden.

requirements.rationale: A waiting run consumes its timeout while the operator is unaware; once the wait has ended there is nothing left to surface.
requirements.statement: Navigation SHALL show, for each listed conversation, whether it is running, waiting on the operator, or idle — waiting meaning it holds an unanswered question still being waited on or a pending permission request — with waiting distinguishable from and outranking running, and a collapsed agent SHALL show when any of its conversations is waiting.

requirements.rationale: Agent settings is a linkable destination with a fixed way back to the agent's most recent conversation, not a dialog.
requirements.statement: Every agent row and conversation row in navigation SHALL expose its actions through a menu opened from a control on the row, reachable by keyboard, shown at rest on the active row and revealed on hover or focus elsewhere; a conversation row SHALL offer rename and archive (unarchive when archived), and an agent row SHALL offer new conversation, agent settings and the archived-conversation listing, with an unavailable item shown disabled with its reason.

requirements.rationale: An abandoned start leaves nothing behind, and a pre-selected agent is a default, not a binding.
requirements.statement: Starting a new conversation SHALL be initiated from navigation and SHALL open a surface whose composer is the primary element, led by a question naming the bound agent (or asking which agent should take the work); the operator SHALL be able to retarget to any project agent, the recency view's start SHALL require choosing an agent before sending, and no conversation record SHALL be created until the first message is sent.

requirements.rationale: A loop firing every few minutes would otherwise fill an agent's list with near-identical rows.
requirements.statement: Navigation SHALL group an agent's consecutive conversations from the same loop's firings into one expandable row, and the display cap SHALL never split such a group.

requirements.rationale: The tree iterates the open roster, so these conversations otherwise vanished while the recency view still listed them.
requirements.statement: Open conversations belonging to an archived agent SHALL be listed in navigation in a marked group of their own, and opening one SHALL offer to unarchive the agent.
